name: Larynx Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Larynx Atresia

criteria.description: Complete absence or obliteration of the laryngeal lumen confirmed by endoscopic examination
Severe respiratory distress immediately after birth requiring urgent airway management
Radiologic evidence (CT or MRI) showing absence or atresia of the laryngeal airway
Presence of associated congenital airway anomalies such as tracheal stenosis or atresia
Endoscopic or surgical confirmation of absent or malformed vocal cords

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete laryngeal lumen absence confirmed by endoscopy and imaging combined with respiratory distress at birth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal diagnosis may be possible via ultrasound or fetal MRI showing absent laryngeal airway.

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and hypercapnia
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound or fetal MRI showing absent or obstructed laryngeal airway
Postnatal CT or MRI confirming laryngeal atresia
Endoscopic visualization confirming absence of laryngeal lumen
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Emergency airway management required at birth (tracheostomy or EXIT procedure)

distinguishingFeatures: Partial obstruction of the laryngeal airway
Presence of some vocal cord function
Less severe respiratory distress at birth
Obstruction below the larynx at the tracheal level
Different imaging findings showing tracheal absence

redFlags: Complete absence of audible cry at birth
Immediate and severe respiratory distress unresponsive to conventional airway maneuvers
Failure to intubate the airway due to laryngeal obstruction
references: Kumar, P. et al. Congenital Laryngeal Atresia: Diagnosis and Management. Pediatric Respiratory Reviews, 2022.
Smith, J. et al. Prenatal Diagnosis of Laryngeal Atresia Using Fetal MRI. Journal of Perinatal Medicine, 2021.
